faq_items.question: Can I print abstract wall art at home, or do I need a print shop?
faq_items.answer: You can print most abstract wall art at home. A standard inkjet on heavyweight matte paper handles sizes up to letter or tabloid beautifully. For larger pieces or the truest color, upload the file to a print shop or a warehouse-club photo counter for just a few dollars.

faq_items.question: What is the best paper for printing wall art?
faq_items.answer: Heavyweight matte cardstock is best. It gives prints a substantial, gallery weight and catches almost no glare, unlike thin, shiny copy paper. Look for a matte or ultra-premium presentation paper in the 60 to 100 pound range at any office or craft store for the most professional finish.

faq_items.question: What size should abstract wall art be above a couch?
faq_items.answer: Art above a sofa should span roughly two-thirds of the couch's width. For most sofas that means an 18x24 or 24x36 print, or a grouping of smaller frames that together cover the same span. When you are between two sizes, size up so the piece does not look lost.

faq_items.question: How do I hang abstract art at the right height?
faq_items.answer: Hang art so its center sits about 57 inches from the floor, the standard gallery eye level. Above furniture, leave 6 to 10 inches between the top of the sofa or headboard and the bottom of the frame so the art relates to the piece below it rather than floating.

faq_items.question: Does abstract wall art have a right way up?
faq_items.answer: Usually not. Abstract art has no fixed orientation or hidden meaning, so you can rotate a print until the composition feels balanced to you. Trust the direction that makes you pause and look. If a design includes text or a clear horizon line, though, follow that cue for the intended orientation.
